lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you with your Child Benefit eligibility, I need to start by understanding the ages of the children you're inquiring about.

**First question: How old are the children you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

This will help me guide you through the right questions. Please tell me:
- The name(s) and age(s) of your child/children

The rules vary depending on age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify automatically
- **16-19**: Need to be in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally don't qualify

Please share the details of the child/children you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 19 years old. I live with Alex and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 19 years old**.

Since Alex is 19, I need to check some additional criteria. For 19-year-olds, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

**Let me navigate to the next question:**

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training situation.

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In approved education or training** (e.g., school, college, university, apprenticeship, or other approved training)?

2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?

3. **Neither** - not in education/training and hasn't recently left?

Please let me know which of these applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education - they're studying for their A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex is in education studying for A-levels at sixth form college. That's helpful information.

Now let me check the specific education level requirements:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I can see that A-levels is one of the **approved education qualifications** for Child Benefit purposes. However, I need to check a few more details to ensure Alex meets all the requirements:

**1. Study hours:** Is Alex studying full-time at sixth form college? (The requirement is at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

**2. Work situation:** Is Alex working full-time? (This could affect eligibility)

**3. Marital status:** Is Alex married?

Please let me know about these details so I can complete the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, Alex is studying full-time at sixth form - definitely more than 12 hours a week of classes and supervised study. 

No, Alex doesn't work full-time - just has a small Saturday job at a local shop to earn some pocket money.

And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for those details. Alex is studying full-time (more than 12 hours per week) for A-levels at sixth form college, has a part-time Saturday job, and isn't married. This is looking positive!

Let me navigate to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! This is straightforward. Since Alex is in approved education (A-levels), the 24-hour work limit is less restrictive. You've already confirmed Alex just works a Saturday job, which is definitely less than 24 hours per week.

Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Or is Alex **not receiving** any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in their own right. They're just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not receiving any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if Alex is in an apprenticeship:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship of any kind?**

Since Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form college (as you mentioned), I'm expecting the answer is "no" - but let me confirm to be thorough.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - no, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship. They're just doing their A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, just studying A-levels at sixth form. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check the claimant's (your) residency situation. There are several possible paths that could make you eligible under UK residency requirements:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path for most people

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - and one of:
   - You're working and earning/expecting to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work (jobseeker), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family financially (and not claiming certain benefits), OR
   - You're studying and have sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Please let me know which applies to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the first one applies to me - I normally live in the UK. I live here in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK in Manchester with Alex. That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. There are a few ways this can be established:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - You're living together in the same household

2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents (at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount)

3. **You're paying maintenance** - You have a court order or formal agreement for maintenance payments

Since you've already mentioned you live with Alex in Manchester, I believe the first option applies. Can you confirm that you live together in the same household?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me in our home in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live together with Alex in your home in Manchester. That clearly establishes your responsibility for them. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important question about other claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative
- Anyone else who lives with Alex or contributes to their upkeep

Or is it just you claiming?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one looking to claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're the only one claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **In hospital** - Currently an inpatient in hospital
2. **In care** - In a residential care facility or children's home
3. **Fostered** - In a fostering arrangement
4. **Normal living** - Living at home with you (as you've described)

Since you've mentioned Alex lives with you at home in Manchester, I believe it's the "normal living" option. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is living normally at home with me. Not in hospital, care, or fostered - just living at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. I just need to check one final thing:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is Alex being supported by you (not by the council)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm supporting Alex myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful! That's the final piece of information I needed. You're supporting Alex yourself, and the local council isn't paying towards their accommodation or maintenance.

Let me navigate to the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need. Let me report your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **GOOD NEWS! YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

I'm pleased to confirm that **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

---

### **Why Alex Qualifies:**

✅ **Age & Education**: Alex is 19 years old and studying for A-levels at sixth form college - this is approved non-advanced education

✅ **Study Commitment**: Alex is studying full-time (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study)

✅ **Work Situation**: Alex works part-time (Saturday job only) - well below the 24-hour working limit

✅ **Benefits**: Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in their own right

✅ **No Apprenticeship**: Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

✅ **Claimant Residency**: You normally live in the UK (Manchester)

✅ **Responsibility**: You live with Alex and are responsible for their upkeep

✅ **No Other Claimants**: You're the only person claiming for Alex

✅ **Council Support**: The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim or **by post using form CH2**

2. **Gather documents you'll need:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Your National Insurance number

3. **Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you (or a partner) earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which reduces or eliminates the benefit. Check if this applies to you.

4. **Payment Schedule:**
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

**For more information:** Visit https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?

reasonings: Alex is 19 years old and in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form college), which qualifies as non-advanced education. Alex is studying full-time (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study), is not working full-time (only a part-time Saturday job, well below the 24-hour limit), is not receiving benefits in their own right (ESA or Universal Credit), and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. The claimant lives in the UK (Manchester), normally resides there, lives with Alex, is the sole person claiming for Alex, Alex lives at home (not in hospital, care, or fostered), and the local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Alex meets all the qualifying criteria as a 19-year-old in approved full-time education (A-levels), with no disqualifying factors. You meet all the claimant requirements as someone who normally lives in the UK, lives with Alex, is responsible for their upkeep, and has no other claimants competing for the same child. There are no barriers to eligibility."
